conviction.explanation: Three of four analysts (fundamentals high, sentiment medium, macro medium) point buy; technicals are neutral. The directional tilt is real — record demand, a leading-edge structural monopoly, self-funded capex, and a forward multiple below the 5-year median — but the debate materially damaged the confidence intervals rather than the direction. Bear won two specific exchanges: the forward multiple is circular (built on consensus EPS from a street with 18/19 buys and zero sells extrapolating +40%), and the 2-4pp gross margin dilution guide is the only forward-looking management signal while the July print is backward-looking and already in the price. Both sides conceded there is no defensible stop at current price (nearest support is inside noise at <0.2 ATR; the next valid one implies ~6.9% drawdown), and that RSI 71.1 makes a single full-size entry poor execution. Score kept well below the 0.7692 cap because entry timing is unfavourable, fair value is unresolved by a wide margin ($326.37 to $542.64 bracketing spot at -21%/+31%), and an unsizable cross-strait tail sits under a crowded consensus.

executive_summary:
TSM is a buy on business quality and demand, not on price or timing. The operating facts are undisputed by either side of the debate: July 2026 revenue of NT$467.58bn (+44.7% YoY) is a record, FY2026 is guided slightly above +40% in USD, margins are 59.9% gross / 50.8% operating / 44.6% net, and $60-64bn of capex (70-80% advanced nodes) is funded entirely from NT$992bn of FCF against 19.9% debt/equity. This is a leading-edge foundry with no functional substitute, expanding into demand it cannot currently meet, without needing external capital. That combination justifies a directional long.

The case against is not about demand — it is about what you pay and what management is telling you about the future. The 18.98x forward multiple is derived from consensus EPS produced by a street with 18/19 buy-or-better ratings and zero sells for four months, all extrapolating +40% growth; the observable trailing multiple is 31.2x against a 22.8x five-year median, a 37% premium. Meanwhile the only genuinely forward-looking management disclosure — 2-4pp of consolidated gross margin dilution from overseas fabs — points down, and it was issued with Arizona's strong H1-26 numbers (NT$36.1bn vs NT$16.1bn for all of FY25) already in hand. That asymmetry matters: the bull's best evidence was known to management when they guided lower. Arizona is one fab, one half-year, at the single site holding a revocable Section 232 exclusion, while Kumamoto and two further 3nm ramps remain pre-profitable. FCF conversion of only 58% of net income is consistent with a finite build-out but is not proof of one.

Timing is the weakest part of the setup and should govern execution. Price at 413.41 sits below the SMA-50 (424.79) after a -4.1% rejection, 13.69% under the 52-week high, with RSI-14 at 71.14 still unwinding, a rally that ran on shrinking volume (9.53M to 6.29M) and a heavier down day — a first lower high on distribution-flavoured tape. Both debaters agreed no defensible stop exists here: the nearest support is inside the noise band and the next valid level implies roughly a 6.9% drawdown. Add a hawkish Fed (9-3 hold, all three dissents wanting a hike, next decision 2026-09-15/16) with beta 1.258, and near-term multiple compression is a live risk even if the thesis is right. Conclusion: own it, size it modestly, scale rather than take one full position, and accept wide drawdown tolerance in exchange for structural exposure. The weaker TWD (~31.94, ~6% softer YoY) is a real but non-thesis translation tailwind.
bull_case: TSM is the sole viable supplier of leading-edge logic at scale, and demand is at a multi-year high while the multiple is not. July revenue +44.7% YoY runs ahead of management's own >+40% FY guide, putting PEG below 0.5x on forward numbers and leaving the forward multiple beneath the 22.8x five-year median. Margin dilution is a percentage phenomenon, not a profit phenomenon: 2-4pp off a 59.9% gross margin on 40%+ volume growth still produces substantially more absolute gross profit, and Arizona's ~4.5x step-change in profitability (NT$36.1bn in H1-26 versus NT$16.1bn for all FY25) suggests new capacity converts to profit faster than models assume. The expansion is self-financed — NT$992bn FCF, 19.9% debt/equity, debt at 0.63x net income, FCF covering total debt in about a year — so 58% FCF conversion reads as greenfield build-out rather than a maintenance treadmill; a treadmill would show rising leverage and falling returns, and neither is present. Policy is a relative advantage: the Jan 2026 US-Taiwan agreement's reduced or excluded Section 232 semiconductor tariffs favour US-expanding chipmakers, and TSM's Arizona capacity is the only leading-edge capacity on US soil, while the 10% Section 122 surcharge is industry-wide. Rate policy barely touches a company funding capex from operating cash flow. GF Value of $326.37 is trailing-anchored on a company mid-inflection. And the cross-strait tail is precisely why this asset trades near 19x forward rather than 40x — the discount is the compensation.
bear_case: The attractive multiple is an artifact of the same unanimity being cited as support. Forward 18.98x is computed off consensus EPS from a street with 18/19 buys, zero sells for four months, and +40% growth extrapolated forward; normalize growth toward 20% and that becomes mid-to-high 20s, against an observable 31.2x trailing versus a 22.8x median. The two management disclosures are not symmetric: the record July print is backward-looking and demonstrably in the price (the market saw it and sold on 08-18, leaving price 13.69% below the 52-week high), while the 2-4pp dilution guide is the sole forward-looking signal and points down — issued across three simultaneous greenfield 3nm ramps in three jurisdictions with different labor, power, and permitting cost bases. Markets pay for margin trajectory, not absolute gross profit. Earnings quality is soft (FCF only 58% of net income) and the $60-64bn is mandatory leading-edge spend, not discretionary; institutions cited exactly this capex escalation while selling. Arizona's strength is one fab, one half-year, at the one site holding a revocable Section 232 exclusion — the relief is a hostage arrangement, and the H200 ban/unban/25%-tariff sequence falsifies any assumption of a rational counterparty. A hawkish 9-3 hold with energy-driven inflation hits both the discount rate and power-intensive fab operating costs at once; with beta 1.258 and a thesis that is explicitly a re-rate toward $542.64, that is thesis risk, not generic timing risk. Technically this is a first lower high — SMA-50 rejection, RSI unwinding from 71, rally on collapsing volume then heavy down volume. And with zero sells and consensus crowded, the cross-strait tail is uncompensated rather than paid for.
key_uncertainties: Whether +40%-plus growth persists into FY2027 or normalizes — this alone determines whether the real forward multiple is ~19x or mid-to-high 20s, and it is the single largest swing factor in the thesis.

Realized consolidated gross margin once Arizona, Kumamoto and the remaining 3nm ramps are fully blended; the guided 2-4pp dilution is the only forward-looking management signal and it was issued with Arizona's strong results already known.
Whether $60-64bn capex intensity is a finite build-out that steps down and lifts FCF conversion above 58%, or a permanent feature of leading-edge competition.
Whether Arizona's profitability is repeatable and site-independent, or partly an artifact of early-ramp economics and its revocable Section 232 exclusion.
Durability of the Jan 2026 US-Taiwan arrangement under an erratic policy regime; the relief is revocable and the 10% Section 122 surcharge remains in force.
Whether energy-driven inflation materially raises operating costs for power-intensive fabs, compounding the guided dilution.
Cross-strait outcome and timing — a real, unsizable binary tail that no valuation exercise in this analysis prices.
Fair value is genuinely unresolved: the street's $542.64 and GuruFocus's $326.37 bracket spot at +31% and -21%, and the debate narrowed the range by nothing.
Whether 08-18 was ordinary profit-taking or institutional distribution — there is no subsequent tape to adjudicate it.
Whether analyst unanimity (zero sells, 18/19 buy-or-better) is confirmation or a crowding signal that removes the marginal buyer.
Whether a risk-managed long is constructible at this price at all, given the nearest support sits inside the noise band and the next valid level implies roughly a 6.9% drawdown.
catalysts_upcoming: FOMC decision 2026-09-15/16 — live hike risk after a hawkish 9-3 hold in which all three dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) wanted a 25bp increase; with beta 1.258 this is the nearest-dated multiple-compression event.
Monthly revenue prints — the August and September releases test whether the July +44.7% YoY pace holds or begins normalizing toward the FY guide.
Next quarterly earnings and gross margin guidance — the first read on whether realized dilution lands inside, below, or above the guided 2-4pp as multiple ramps blend in.
Any update on 2027 capex intensity — a step-down would validate the finite-build-out reading and lift FCF conversion; another escalation supports the treadmill case.
Further disclosure on Arizona and first signs of Kumamoto profitability — the test of whether Arizona's step-change generalizes across sites.
US policy action on Section 232 exclusions or the 10% Section 122 surcharge — revocation or extension directly re-rates the tariff-moat argument.
China export-licensing decisions and Taiwan's 279-entity watch list — continued erratic sequencing (as with H200) keeps a discount on the multiple.
Technical resolution of the 419.63-424.79 zone versus loss of the 410 area — the tape event that adjudicates profit-taking versus distribution and materially improves or worsens entry.
USD/TWD trajectory around ~31.94 — sustained TWD weakness continues as a translation tailwind on largely USD-denominated sales.
